**SECTION B - COMPOSITION (40 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (12 marks); Expression (16 marks); Accuracy (12 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write on from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 450 - 500 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** Tell a story to illustrate the proverb: *Prevention is better than cure.*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: state the proverb and introduce the main character.
2. Warning ignored: a trader neglects a simple precaution.
3. The disaster that follows.
4. The cost of the cure compared with the cost of prevention.
5. Conclusion: the moral of the story.

**Model composition (473 words)**

There is an old saying that prevention is better than cure, and I understood its meaning very clearly through the story of my uncle, Mr Fon, who was a proud and stubborn trader in our village.

Mr Fon owned a large shop, in which he sold rice, oil, sugar and a lot of other goods. The shop was old, and the electric wires in the ceiling were worn out and uncovered. Several times, the electrician who had wired the building had warned him. "Mr Fon, these wires are dangerous," he said. "Let me change them before they cause a fire. It will cost only fifty thousand francs." My uncle waved his hand. "Why should I waste money on something that works?" he replied. "The shop has stood there for twenty years, and nothing has happened."

My aunt also begged him to buy a fire extinguisher and to put out the lights at night, but he laughed at her. "You women worry too much," he said. He thought that to spend money on safety was a waste, so he put the matter aside.

One stormy night in the dry season, I was sleeping in the room behind the shop when I woke up with a strange smell. I opened the door and saw thick smoke and red flames climbing the wall near the ceiling. "Fire! Fire!" I screamed. The neighbours rushed out with buckets of water, but the fire spread quickly because the shop was full of cartons, bags of sugar and cans of oil. Within an hour, the whole building was burning, and the villagers could only stand and watch as the roof fell in.

By morning, all that remained was a heap of black ashes. Mr Fon sat on the ground with his head in his hands, and tears rolled down his cheeks. He had lost goods worth more than ten million francs, and he had no insurance. The money which he might have saved by refusing to repair the wires had cost him everything he had worked for. Moreover, he had to borrow money to start again, and it took him five years to pay the debt.

When he finally opened a small stall by the road, he called the electrician himself and asked him to check every wire. He bought two fire extinguishers and taught his workers to use them. He also told his story to every trader who came near his shop. "I ignored a small warning, and I paid a big price," he used to say. "A stitch in time would have saved me nine."

From my uncle's experience, I learnt that it is wiser and cheaper to prevent a problem than to repair it. Whether it concerns health, farming, studies or business, a little care today saves a great loss tomorrow. Indeed, prevention is better than cure.

**Marking grid**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 12 | Relevant ideas that answer the topic, developed with examples, in clear paragraphs with an introduction and a conclusion |
| Expression | 16 | Varied vocabulary and sentence structures, appropriate style and tone, fluent links between ideas |
| Accuracy | 12 | Correct grammar, tenses, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. A story that does not illustrate the proverb: the moral must be shown by what happens, not only stated at the end.
2. Telling the moral in the first line and then ignoring it in the story.
